derived_opportunities.reason: No technically reliable standalone published skill survived review; accepted engine packs discuss deadlocks only as a subsection.
derived_opportunities.potential_value: High: a wait-for-graph, victim, retry, and lock-order workflow would prevent misleading permanent-hang diagnoses.
derived_opportunities.notes: Keep engine-specific detection and victim semantics explicit; do not invent a published skill from documentation.

derived_opportunities.reason: Broad concurrency skills were found, but no focused cross-ORM procedure covers version columns, SQL Server rowversion, HTTP ETags, JPA @Version, EF tokens, and DynamoDB conditional writes.
derived_opportunities.potential_value: High: catches silent lost updates across APIs and ORM layers.
derived_opportunities.notes: The accepted Database Concurrency Audit gives partial coverage, so this opportunity is for a narrower implementation-and-test workflow.

derived_opportunities.reason: Redis and general database sources discuss locks, but no qualifying published skill validates monotonically increasing fencing tokens and stale-holder rejection.
derived_opportunities.potential_value: High: prevents stale lock holders from mutating protected resources after lease expiry.
derived_opportunities.notes: Do not reduce the workflow to Redlock acquisition; downstream resource enforcement is the missing core.

derived_opportunities.reason: Published PostgreSQL skills mention advisory locks, but no standalone workflow covers key design, session versus transaction scope, leak prevention, pooling, and observability.
derived_opportunities.potential_value: Medium-high: advisory-lock misuse can serialize unrelated tenants or leak locks through pooled sessions.
derived_opportunities.notes: Engine semantics differ; a future workflow should branch explicitly.

derived_opportunities.reason: Official Firebase agent skills cover Firestore and SQL Connect, but no dedicated Realtime Database skill was verified.
searches_attempted: firebase realtime data modeling agent skill
derived_opportunities.potential_value: Medium: denormalized fan-out writes, rules, offline behavior, and query limits differ materially from Firestore.
derived_opportunities.notes: Ordinary Firebase documentation is not a published skill and remains only source material.

derived_opportunities.reason: Official D1 guidance is nested reference material, while the two standalone community candidates failed safety and currency review.
derived_opportunities.potential_value: High: remote migration ordering, partial failure, bindings, backups, and rollback need a safe executable contract.
derived_opportunities.notes: Do not split Cloudflare reference pages into invented catalog entries.

derived_opportunities.reason: Turso and SQLite/D1 audit skills provide partial coverage, but no accurate standalone SQLite concurrency and recovery workflow passed review.
derived_opportunities.potential_value: High for embedded and edge applications that mis-handle writer contention and checkpoint growth.
derived_opportunities.notes: Reject unqualified throughput multipliers and obsolete sqlite-vss recommendations.

derived_opportunities.reason: Amazon Keyspaces supplies strong Cassandra-compatible guidance, but no provider-neutral Cassandra skill was verified.
derived_opportunities.potential_value: Medium-high: query-first modeling, partition sizing, tombstones, and consistency levels are easy to misapply.
derived_opportunities.notes: Keep Keyspaces-specific compatibility separate from portable Cassandra semantics.

derived_opportunities.reason: No credible ScyllaDB-specific published skill survived organization, registry, code, and gap searches.
derived_opportunities.potential_value: Medium: shard-aware drivers, partition sizing, and workload-specific differences deserve explicit treatment.
derived_opportunities.notes: scylla-cluster-tests results are project testing infrastructure, not reusable application skills.

derived_opportunities.reason: Official MongoDB skills are driver and database focused; no credible Mongoose-specific reusable skill was verified.
derived_opportunities.potential_value: Medium-high: populate behavior, lean reads, middleware, discriminators, and transaction sessions create ORM-specific risks.
derived_opportunities.notes: Do not relabel generic MongoDB guidance as Mongoose expertise.

derived_opportunities.reason: Redis coverage is deep, but no trustworthy KeyDB-specific published skill was found.
derived_opportunities.potential_value: Medium: compatibility, active replication, and multi-threaded behavior should not be inferred from Redis alone.
derived_opportunities.notes: A future published workflow should clearly scope supported KeyDB versions.

derived_opportunities.reason: Engine and provider skills discuss backup and restore, but no provider-neutral skill verifies logical correctness, constraints, sequences, permissions, RPO, and application smoke after restore.
derived_opportunities.potential_value: High: backup success without restore correctness is a common false assurance.
derived_opportunities.notes: The accepted MariaDB and Neon/PostgreSQL sources are engine-specific, not this cross-engine audit.

waves.name: Existing atlas baseline
waves.notes: Inspected all 20 Databases-category records plus adjacent Redis, EF Core, Django, JPA, migration, and storage entries; 14 records warranted metadata corrections.

waves.name: Official database agent-skill repositories
waves.notes: Opened canonical official repositories for MongoDB, Qdrant, Redis, Neon, MariaDB, PlanetScale, Prisma, Neo4j Contrib, Turso, and YugabyteDB.

waves.name: skills.sh and registries
waves.notes: Ran 26 skills.sh database/task query families with top-100 windows; registry rows were discovery leads only and were never counted as reviewed candidates until canonical triage.

waves.name: GitHub repository search
waves.notes: Ran 29 repository-search queries across engines, databases, skills, ORM ecosystems, migrations, and query performance; raw result counts were not promoted into candidate totals.

waves.name: GitHub code search
waves.notes: Ran 30 authenticated code-search executions across engine and failure terms, including six rate-limit attempts that were retried; candidate counting began only after file-level triage.

waves.name: Database vendor organizations
waves.notes: Inspected vendor organizations and exact repository trees for database and vector engines; downstream plugin packaging was separated from canonical leaves.

waves.name: ORM and query-builder organizations
waves.notes: Searched Prisma, Drizzle, SQLAlchemy, Django ORM, EF Core, Hibernate, jOOQ, Eloquent, ActiveRecord, GORM, Diesel, SeaORM, SQLx, Knex, Kysely, and sqlc surfaces.

waves.name: Cloud and database providers
waves.notes: Reviewed AWS, Firebase, Vercel, Neon, Supabase, Turso, Azure-adjacent, and managed database workflows; provisioning-primary material was rejected.

waves.name: Database performance specialists
waves.notes: Inspected query-plan, indexing, PgBouncer, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Grafana, and operational-performance specialists with a factual-correctness gate.

waves.name: Awesome lists and curated collections
waves.notes: Used GitHub Awesome Copilot and curated collections for discovery, then traced every accepted entry to a direct canonical blob and rejected defective helpers.

waves.name: Maintainer snowballing
waves.notes: Snowballed from maintainers and skill references into event4u, Sigistry, Convex, sql2er, and focused data-access repositories.

waves.name: Social and community discovery
waves.notes: Used publicly indexed community results only; no account-gated social interaction was attempted and no skill was accepted solely from a social claim.

waves.name: Multilingual discovery
waves.notes: Executed Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Spanish, Portuguese, French, and German searches. The unique accepted addition was the ten-skill official Hologres cluster; 12 Aliyun AIOps candidates remained deferred.

waves.name: Long-tail database failures
waves.notes: Targeted deadlocks, N+1, SKIP LOCKED, keyset pagination, backups, restore, bloat, pooling, migrations, and long-tail failure signatures.

waves.name: Gap-driven second pass
waves.notes: Re-ran targeted searches for underrepresented MySQL, SQLite, libSQL, D1, MongoDB, DynamoDB, Firestore, SQL Server, and ORM gaps.

waves.name: Saturation, canonicalization, and dedupe audit
waves.notes: Compared locators, names, descriptions, paths, source trees, and known adapter hashes; retained canonical leaves and documented every grouped mirror count.
